chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said:

I asked him about the Magians: what is their legal status? He said: “They are from the People of the Book, and their ruling is like the ruling of the Jews and the Christians concerning prescribed punishments and blood-money.”

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: the People of the Book, a recognized scriptural community in Islamic law
key_terms.الدِّيَاتِ: blood-money or financial compensation for injury or killing
key_terms.النَّصَارَى: the Christians, used here as a point of legal comparison
key_terms.الْمَجُوسِ: the Magians, a religious community discussed in legal classification
key_terms.الْيَهُودِ: the Jews, used here as a point of legal comparison
key_terms.مَجْرَاهُمْ: their legal course or applicable ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of the Magians in Shiʿi hadith regarding prescribed punishments and blood-money?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding the Magians, identifying them as being among the People of the Book. It further establishes that, in the matters of prescribed punishments and blood-money, their legal treatment follows that of the Jews and Christians.
